chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Ubayd, from Yunus, from a man, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
Leave your son to play for seven years, and impose yourself (upon him) for seven. So if he succeeds (fine), or else he is from the ones who have no good in them.

key_terms.أَلْزِمْهُ: impose upon him / make him adhere

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic method for raising children according to the Imams?
ai.summary: In Shia tradition, this hadith from Al-Kafi is often interpreted through the lens of developmental psychology, where the first seven years (Sinn al-Lu'ub) prioritize emotional bonding and joy to establish a secure attachment, while the subsequent seven years (Sinn al-Adab) introduce structured discipline and moral education. This two-phase model underscores the Imams' emphasis on balancing affection with authority, suggesting that early neglect of play can hinder later receptiveness to guidance. The concluding remark about 'no good in him' if he fails reflects the potential for moral decline when foundational character building is mishandled.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from Muhammad Bin Isa Bin Ubeyd, from Yunus, from a man, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘Leave your son to play for seven years, and impose yourself (upon him) for seven. So if he succeeds (fine), or else he is from the ones who have no good in them’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from Muhammad ibn ‘Isa ibn ‘Ubayd from Yunus from a man who has said the following: “Abu ‘ Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘

Allow your child to play for seven years and keep him with yourself for another seven years (to practice and behave as you do) if he succeeds; otherwise, he is of the ones in whom there is nothing good.’”
